title: Potiphar's House
reflectionText: Four times the story stops to say the same thing: Yahweh was with Joseph. He was with him when Joseph rose to run the house, and he was with him just as much when a lie sent him down to the prison. The favor did not keep him from the false accusation; it followed him into the cell. What is it to be accompanied like that — not spared the fall, but never left in it?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch B (Full-Canon Production Gate CG19, rescoped and owner-approved). Genesis 39 ONLY — Genesis 40 is deliberately excluded (already covered by 1178 and 1389, so any inclusion would duplicate), and Joseph's later prison interpretation work is not shown. Fills the Joseph adult-arc middle between the coat (1037) and the reveal (1003). SHORT+FULL (WEB 335w/501w; KJV 351w/520w). The repeated source refrain 'Yahweh was with Joseph' (39:2, 39:3, 39:21, 39:23) is preserved as the story's spine in every variant. Potiphar's wife's false accusation handled exactly and NOT softened: her claim that the Hebrew came in to mock/lie with her and fled leaving his garment when she cried out is kept faithful (39:14-15, 39:17-18). No invented attraction, motive, private thought, gesture, or emotional state — the text states only that she 'set her eyes on Joseph' and said 'Lie with me'; Joseph's stated reason (his master's trust, sinning against God, 39:8-9) is kept; 'well-built and handsome' is source-stated (39:6). Ends within Genesis 39 on the complete shape (prosperity in the prison, 39:21-23). KJV lane uses KJV diction (the Lord, goodly person and well favoured, grace); WEB uses Yahweh.
